subject.title: fix(codex): cap compaction override warning cache via createDedupeCache

question: Should the Codex ignored-compaction-override warning re-warn after an arbitrary 4096-key eviction despite its configuration-derived key space and existing process-lifetime warn-once behavior?
rationale: The implementation and proof are sound, but repository policy and the closely related owner decision make the diagnostic lifecycle tradeoff a human ownership choice rather than a correctness question automation can settle.

options.title: Require measured need
options.body: Keep the current Set unless production evidence or a realistic owner-path reproduction demonstrates harmful key growth and supports a lifecycle-derived bound or reset.

options.title: Accept bounded re-warning
options.body: Approve the 4096-entry cache as an intentional memory-versus-diagnostic tradeoff and accept repeated warnings after eviction.

options.title: Use owner lifecycle reset
options.body: Reset or bound warning state at the canonical agent or configuration registry lifecycle instead of applying generic LRU eviction.

recommendation.title: Require measured need
recommendation.body: Keep the current Set unless production evidence or a realistic owner-path reproduction demonstrates harmful key growth and supports a lifecycle-derived bound or reset.
